clue.text: Homer's song about quiet brother and sister

parts.note: a homer is a homing pigeon
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Homer's song portrays a quiet young brother and sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' suggests the poet (or Simpson); here it is a homing pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon pair is a British expression for twins, or a family's only two children, one boy and one girl.

clue.text: I rabbit on initially about people in opera

indicators.note: the rabbit word goes round the people

parts.note: a doe is a female rabbit
men means people

indicators.note: only the opening letter of on is used

explanation.surface: I keep rabbiting on about people at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit on' looks like the British idiom for chattering; 'rabbit' is DOE and 'on' gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idomeneo is an opera by Mozart.

clue.text: Organ: what Cockney does with it

definitions.meaning: a body part used for hearing
a Cockney drops the H of hear, saying it without that letter

explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is the organ of hearing, and 'ear is how a Cockney says hear, which is what one does with it.

clue.text: Worst moment, laughing almost over; depression's starting to set in

indicators.note: the starting letter is put inside the turned word
over signals the word is turned backwards
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: riant means laughing or cheerful

indicators.note: only the start of the word depression is taken

explanation.surface: At the worst moment, laughter is nearly over and depression begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops T from RIANT, 'over' turns RIAN to NAIR, and 'to set in' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, so a person's worst moment.

clue.text: Not easy to find couple in a hurry — husband's gone off

indicators.note: the couple sits inside the rest
has gone off means the husband letter leaves

parts.note: a rush is a hurry
a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: A couple in a hurry find it hard after the husband has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone off' takes H from A RUSH to leave ARUS; DUO goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arduous means hard and laborious, so not easy.

clue.text: Torture, then point to tree being prepared for criminal

parts.note: to rack is to torture
E is a compass point

indicators.note: the tree's letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A criminal tortures someone then points to a tree being got ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer is a criminal running an illegal business or extortion racket.

clue.text: Leader of gang better off at first

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word off is taken

explanation.surface: A gang leader is better off from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo is the head of a Mafia family or criminal crew.

clue.text: Family fated to be cut off in secret

parts.note: a clan is a family group

indicators.note: the end letter is cut off

parts.note: destined means fated

explanation.surface: A family is fated to be cut off in secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Clandestine means done in secret, concealed.

clue.text: Accommodation not yet brilliant?

parts.note: pre means before, so not yet
fab is slang for fabulous, brilliant

explanation.surface: Lodgings that are not yet brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: A prefab is a prefabricated house, common in post-war Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Travelled wearing fabric with holes in?

indicators.note: the travelling word is clothed in the fabric, so the fabric goes round it

parts.note: cord is short for corduroy, a ribbed cloth
rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone rode about in a fabric outfit that had holes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eaten away by rust or chemicals is left pitted, with holes in it, as the question mark concedes.

clue.text: Fit into court house

indicators.note: the fitness word is put inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: hale means healthy and fit

explanation.surface: Instructions to fit something into a courthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden house of the Swiss Alpine type, so a kind of house.

clue.text: Struggle in speech with stuff about a republic

indicators.note: the struggle word is heard as it would be pronounced in German, where W is said like V

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: the stuffing word is turned backwards

parts.note: to ram is to cram or stuff

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to talk about the stuff of a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: German says W as V, so WEI sounds like VIE; 'about' turns RAM to MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is the usual short name for the German Republic of 1919 to 1933, named after the city where its constitution was drafted.

clue.text: Sweet senior officer about a metre — not tall!

indicators.note: the officer goes round the metre

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking officer
low means not tall

explanation.surface: A sweet senior officer is about a metre high, so not tall.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshmallow is a soft spongy sweet.

clue.text: Add detail too thickly, so unbalance one's account

definitions.meaning: to draw over-heavily, exaggerating detail in a picture
to take more out of a bank account than it holds

explanation.walkthrough: The held text has a stray 'S ance' from a line break; the page prints 'unbalance' whole. 'so' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdraw means both to exaggerate in drawing and to withdraw more money than a bank balance holds.

clue.text: Perhaps resists witches

parts.note: the letters of sisters, made weird (jumbled), give this word, so it is an example of the reading

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone resists witches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' says the clue word is an example: RESISTS is SISTERS made WEIRD, i.e. scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weird Sisters are the three witches in Shakespeare's Macbeth.

clue.text: Taking action in court about two minutes speech there?

indicators.note: the legal action goes round the minutes

parts.note: suing is taking legal action
M is the abbreviation for minute, twice
up means appearing in court, as in up before the judge

explanation.surface: Suing someone, then a two-minute speech in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to court: a judge's summing-up is a speech there.
explanation.definitionFit: A summing up is the judge's speech to the jury reviewing the evidence at the end of a trial.

clue.text: Artist pretending to be brave in the dark?

definitions.text: pretending to be brave in the dark?
definitions.meaning: someone whistling in the dark to keep up their courage

explanation.definitionFit: Whistler was a painter, and whistling in the dark is feigning courage.

clue.text: Final stage in preparing the histogram

indicators.note: preparing means working the letters of these words up into something new

explanation.surface: The last step in drawing up a histogram.
explanation.definitionFit: The home straight is the last stretch of a racecourse, so figuratively the final stage of any task.

clue.text: Using spades, laboriously moves bundles

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
heaves means lifts or moves with effort

explanation.surface: With spades, someone laboriously shifts bundles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheaves are bundles of grain stalks tied together.

clue.text: Most colourful but subtle arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement here is a reordering of the letters

explanation.surface: The most colourful yet subtle flower arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue language is risqué, colourful talk, so the bluest is the most colourful.

clue.text: Run around a little in mild irritation

indicators.note: the running word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a bit is a little

explanation.surface: Running around a little causes slight irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleabite is figuratively any trivial annoyance or minor irritation.

clue.text: Like to break dull sort of spoon

indicators.note: the comparison word breaks into the colour word

parts.note: grey means dull and cheerless
as means like, in comparisons

explanation.surface: Something like a dull spoon is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'greasy spoon' is a cheap British café.
explanation.definitionFit: A greasy spoon is a cheap, grubby café, so greasy describes that sort of spoon.

clue.text: Not all the same logic turned up in robot

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read upwards, backwards
only part of the words is used

explanation.surface: Not all robots share the same logic.
explanation.definitionFit: A golem is a clay figure brought to life in Jewish folklore, hence an automaton or robot.

clue.text: Disorientation of black girl whirling round

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black

indicators.note: the girl word is spun to read backwards

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl in black whirls round until she is disoriented.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is the tiredness and disorientation felt after flying across time zones.

clue.text: Sal's follower of unpredictable temper

definitions.meaning: the second word of the name for smelling salts, whose first word is sal
liable to sudden changes of mood

explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost 'temper' over a column break; the page has it. Sal volatile is an old name for smelling salts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word follows sal in sal volatile, and also describes a person liable to sudden changes of mood.

clue.text: Be likely to drop name, a short one

indicators.note: the name letter is removed

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be likely to

explanation.surface: Someone likely to drop names, even short ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short one' refers back to name: TED is the short form of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted is a shortened form of Edward or Theodore, so a short name.

clue.text: Pack, having journey between two points?

parts.note: S and W are two points of the compass
a journey between places goes from one to another, read as the word to
the second of the two compass points

explanation.surface: Packing for a trip between two places.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'journey between two points' as 'S to W', a trip from south to west.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack goods away neatly.

clue.text: Whitehall warriors come through gate in such style

indicators.note: the warriors pass inside the gate

parts.note: a postern is a back or side gate
MOD is the Ministry of Defence, based in Whitehall, the London street of government offices

explanation.surface: Civil servants march through a gate in a particular fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Postmodern is a style of art and architecture reacting against modernism.
